title: Expressive Asset
description: Metadata contract for a single asset in the Expressive Assets library. Every field here has to earn its place at 500+ assets: identity that never breaks, enough text to make the thing findable, one lifecycle axis, and a trail back to the Figma source.

id.description: Stable, globally unique identifier. Format: <collection>.<slug>. Never change this once published — every consumer references it, and a rename is a breaking change. Change `name` instead and add the old one to `aliases`.

name.description: Human-readable display name shown in the browser UI.

aliases.description: Names this asset used to have, or is commonly called. Search matches against these, so a rename never makes an asset unfindable for the people who learned the old name.

keywords.description: Search terms, especially synonyms someone would type who does not know the asset's name. At 500+ assets this is the difference between a library and a folder of SVGs.

description.description: One line: what the artwork depicts and when to reach for it. Doubles as the duplicate-detector — two assets with the same description are usually the same idea drawn twice.

collection.description: Sub-collection within the type. Extend this list as new collections are added — it is deliberately open to growth.

product.description: For product artwork only: which product it represents (e.g. "Outlook", "Xbox"). Absent for systemic artwork.

status.description: The single lifecycle axis. draft = in progress, do not ship. published = approved for use. deprecated = still present for back-compat, must not be used in new work.

replacedBy.description: Asset id that supersedes this one. Required when status is deprecated — a deprecation with no migration target just strands consumers.

themes.description: Rendered theme variants that exist on disk. standard is the full-colour base; outline and filled are the monochrome reductions. The keys match what the UI shows, so nothing means two things in two places.

sizes.description: Pixel sizes the artwork is designed to read correctly at — not the sizes it can technically scale to. If it turns to mud at 12px, do not list 12.

colors.description: Brand colours baked into the standard variant.

recolorable.description: Whether the artwork may be retinted to a Windows accent. Set false for trademarked brand marks that must ship in their own colors — the browser disables the accent picker for those, so nobody ships a magenta Excel icon.

variants.description: Artwork paths, keyed by theme and then by the pixel size the drawing was made for. Windows product icons are REDRAWN per size — the 16px Excel icon is a different drawing from the 48px one, not a scaled copy — so each is stored separately. Artwork that is genuinely size-agnostic (a single scalable drawing) uses the one key "any". Top-level keys must match the themes array.

figma.description: Where this artwork came from upstream. At 500+ assets, being able to jump from a file on disk back to the component that produced it is not optional.

source.description: Upstream provenance for artwork the library did not draw. Required in practice for anything vendored from a third-party project — the licence obligation travels with the file, not with the README, and an asset that cannot name where it came from cannot be audited later.

owner.description: GitHub handle or team responsible for this asset.

version.description: Semver for the artwork itself. Minor for a redraw, major for a shape change that breaks visual continuity.

updated.description: ISO date of the last artwork change.

notes.description: Usage guidance, restrictions, or redraw history.
